gospel_data.title: Needs: A Biblical Perspective

subsections.title: Common Views of Needs Within Marriage

nestedSubsections.title: A popular book on marriage, such as “Love & Respect,” teach that “the wife primarily needs to feel love and the husband
nestedSubsections.content:
A popular book on marriage, such as “Love & Respect,” teach that “the wife primarily needs to feel love and the husband primarily needs to feel respect.”1 These are called “basic needs.”2

  1. Dr. Eggerichs teaches that when a wife does not feel loved by her husband, she will treat him disrespectfully. Likewise, when a husband does not feel respected by his wife, he will treat her unlovingly. According to this book, when husbands and wives do not get their needs met, they begin a cycle of mistreating each other.

nestedSubsections.title: Another popular book about marriage is “His Needs, Her Needs” by Dr. Willard Harley.
nestedSubsections.content:
1. The husband’s five basic needs are sexual fulfillment, recreational companionship, an attractive spouse, domestic support, and admiration.

  2. The wife’s five basic needs are affection, conversation, honesty and openness, financial support, and family commitment.

nestedSubsections.title: According to these theories, when the basic needs are met, marriages go smoothly, but the marriage is in trouble when their needs are lacking.
nestedSubsections.content:
1. In His Needs, Her Needs, it states a husband has a “compelling need for sex.”3 The word “compel” is a strong word.

    1. To “compel” is to secure or bring about by force. Is this saying a man’s need for sex is so strong he is compelled or forced to meet this need?

nestedSubsections.title: Needs:
nestedSubsections.content:
Needs are defined as a requirement, a necessity, to be necessary, to be under necessity. A genuine need is something that is an imperative requirement.
Matthew 6:31 Do not worry then, saying, “What will we eat?” or “What will we drink?” or “What will we wear for clothing?” For the Gentiles eagerly seek all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
1 Timothy 6:8 If we have food and covering, with these we shall be content.

  1. There is no place in Scripture where sex is called or considered a need.
    1 Thessalonians 4:3-5 God wants you to be holy, so you should keep clear of all sexual sin. Then each of you will control your body and live in holiness and honor--not in lustful passion as the pagans do, in their ignorance of God and his ways.

    1. The Bible tells us to keep clear of all sexual sin, control our body, and live in holiness and honor. Sex is not a need; it is a desire we must control!

  2. There is no place in Scripture where financial security is called or considered a need.
    1 Timothy 6:10 For the love of money is at the root of all kinds of evil. And some people, craving money, have wandered from the faith and pierced themselves with many sorrows.

    1. Financial security is not a need, it is a desire, and we must keep it in perspective.

  3. There is no place in Scripture where having an attractive wife is called or considered a need.
    Proverbs 31:30 Charm is deceitful and beauty is vain, But a woman who fears the LORD, she shall be praised.

    1. An attractive wife is not a need. It may be a desire, but it must be kept in perspective if it is.

  4. Popular self-help books might label sex, affection, financial security, attractiveness, love, respect as needs, but the Bible doesn’t! In truth, they are not needs; they are desires.

subsections.title: When Desires are Viewed as Needs, Problems Arise.

nestedSubsections.title: When a person believes that what they desire is a need:
nestedSubsections.content:
1. They may feel angry when that “need” is not met.

  2. They may feel like a victim.

  3. They may become resentful if their “need” is not fulfilled.

nestedSubsections.title: Viewing Sex as a desire, rather than a need:
nestedSubsections.content:
1. They may respond differently when they receive it and when they don’t receive it.

  2. They should be grateful that someone loves them and that they have covenanted with them in marriage.

nestedSubsections.title: To call a desire a need is to invite anger, discontentment, resentment, bitterness, and all kinds of sinful thoughts, attitudes, and actions.
nestedSubsections.content: 1. You become self-centered, self-focused, and you will do things that are self-destructive, such as sinning against God and your spouse to meet these so-called needs.

nestedSubsections.title: The Problem when you view desires as needs:
nestedSubsections.content:
1. When our desires become so strong that they control us, rather than us controlling them, we get into trouble.
    James 4:1-4 What is causing the quarrels and fights among you? Isn’t it the whole army of evil desires at war within you? You want what you don’t have, so you scheme and kill to get it. You are jealous for what others have, and you can’t possess it, so you fight and quarrel to take it away from them. And yet the reason you don’t have what you want is that you don’t ask God for it. And even when you do ask, you don’t get it because your whole motive is wrong-- you want only what will give you pleasure. You adulterers! Don’t you realize that friendship with this world makes you an enemy of God? I say it again, that if your aim is to enjoy this world, you can’t be a friend of God.

  2. One of the main causes of fights and quarrels among married people is that they have desires that are not being met.

    1. Many marriages are “killed” by divorce because a person wants what they want, and is willing to divorce if they can’t get it.

  3. The way we know a desire has become too strong is this:

    1. If we want something so much that we are willing to sin in order to get it, or to sin if we don’t get it, our desire has become inordinate.

    2. Dr Stuart Scott says, “We worship what we believe we desperately need or must have in order to be happy. When we place this kind of emphasis on something, it is actually a sinful lust.”4

    3. The Bible teaches us that our greatest desire should be to please God.
      2 Corinthians 5:9 Therefore we also have as our ambition, whether at home or absent, to be pleasing to Him.
      Philippians 4:11 Not that I speak from want, for I have learned to be content in whatever circumstances I am.
      1 Timothy 6:6 But godliness actually is a means of great gain when accompanied by contentment.

subsections.title: What Needs Do We Really Have?

nestedSubsections.title: What does everyone actually need according to the Bible?
nestedSubsections.content:
1. The primary need of all husbands and wives, indeed, the primary need for all people is Jesus Christ. Having Jesus Christ as your Lord and Savior is indeed a need!
    Acts 4:12 And there is salvation in no one else; for there is no other name under heaven that has been given among men by which we must be saved.

  2. Without Christ, there is no hope for salvation or reconciliation.
    Hebrews 10:27 There will be nothing to look forward to but the terrible expectation of God’s judgment and the raging fire that will consume his enemies.

  3. What needs do married people actually have, according to the Bible?
    Ecclesiastes 12:13-14 The conclusion, when all has been heard, is: fear God and keep His commandments, because this applies to every person. For God will bring every act to judgment, everything which is hidden, whether it is good or evil.
    Romans 14:12 So then each one of us will give an account of himself to God.

nestedSubsections.title: What needs do married people actually have, according to the Bible?
nestedSubsections.content:
1. Husbands:
    Ephesians 5:25 Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the church and gave Himself up for her.

    1. God has commanded husbands to love their wives as Christ loves the church.

    2. Husbands will one day stand before God and give an account of how they loved your wife!

  2. Wives:
    Ephesians 5:33 Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.
    Ephesians 5:22 Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord.

    1. God has commanded wives to reverence their husbands.

      1. Wives will one day stand before God and give an account of how they reverenced and submitted to their husbands!

  3. As a Christian, your greatest need is to fear God and to keep His commandments.

    1. This means that:

      1. Husbands don’t need to be reverenced, but they NEED to love.

      2. Wives don’t need to be loved, but they NEED to respect.

    2. Your deepest and most basic need is to fear God and keep His commandments. In a marriage that looks like this:

      1. As a husband, you NEED to love your wife as Christ loved the church. As a wife, you NEED to submit to your husband as to the Lord, and you NEED to reverence him. These indeed are genuine needs!

  1. Emerson Eggerichs, Love & Respect: The Love She Most Desires, The Respect He Desperately Needs, 17.

  2. Ibid.

  3. Willard F. Harley, Jr., His Needs, Her Needs: Building an Affair-Proof Marriage, 60.

  4. Stuart Scott, Exemplary Husband, 91.

subsections.title: Homework Questions
subsections.content: Complete the exercises below and save your answers.

questions.question: Memory Verse: Ecclesiastes 12:13-14 The conclusion, when all has been heard, is: fear God and keep His commandments, because this applies to every person. For God will bring every act to judgment, everything which is hidden, whether it is good or evil.

Scripture: Read James 4:1-4 with your spouse and answer the question, “What desires have I had that have caused quarrels and fighting in our marriage?”

  • Ask yourself, “What desires has my spouse had that I have not been willing to fulfill?” Is there any Biblical reason why you cannot begin to fulfill his/her desires right now?
Review and discuss this lesson with your spouse.
Pray daily to love your spouse and to be a better companion.

Application

  • Make a list of at least 30 or more ways that you have sinned against your husband/wife. Keep this list for the next session.
